cases.name: The She-Wolf
cases.source_observation: BALaT identifies Maison La Louve, Grand-Place 5; the photo represents the facade facing the square. No reviewer style label assigned.
cases.source_style_text: Façade with 4 very elongated levels under a pediment in the antique style, reflecting a very modern style at the time of its construction. Elaborate decorative program, primarily devoted to the theme of vice and virtue. Speaking signboard, probably original, by Marc De Vos. The god Apollo with his bow on the pediment, and phoenix at the top, the symbol of rebirth by fire. Ironwork on the doors with intertwining letters of the first names "Antonius" and "Sebastianus", the patron saints of archers.

cases.name: The Fox

cases.source_style_text: Façade with 2 high floors on a base with ground floor and mezzanine, finished with a baroque gable. Complex decorative program on the theme of commerce with: house emblem, 4 reliefs, allegories of the 4 corners of the world surrounding Justice, the year of construction and a statue of Saint Nicolas at the top of the gable. The 4 bas-reliefs, which appear to be originals from the late 17th century, illustrate a haberdashery shop, a draper's shop, a dyeing workshop and a ceramics factory.

cases.name: The Swan
cases.source_observation: Commons category 'The Swan, Brussels' and monument record 2043-0065/009; source-stated Grand-Place identity matched to City dataset record 009 (The Swan). No reviewer style label assigned.
cases.source_style_text: Restrained and monumental façade, in the classical French style, topped by a domed roof finished with a belvedere. Originally, the figurative program was limited to the speaking signboard and monogram of the owner Pierre Fariseau. The Guild of Butchers completed this program with allegories of Agriculture and Butchery on either side of a statue of Abundance, on the pediment of the house. The restorers of the 19th century respected this extended program.

cases.source_style_text: Façade with 3 registers, with restrained ornamentation, and a gable with inverted consoles in the Baroque style. Decorative program with speaking signboard and two bas-reliefs illustrating the work of arms manufacture, inspired by 17th century originals.
